event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: The filing, published in February 2022, discusses COVID-19 less as a one-off shock and more as a still-evolving systemic hazard that touches virtually every operating lever of KO’s business: revenue generation (shift to at-home channels, away-from-home weakness), supply-chain continuity (ingredient shortages, logistics delays, plant shutdowns and cost inflation), labour availability, and macro-economic demand erosion.  Statements span both realised impacts (2020–2021 sales declines, cost increases, asynchronous recovery) and forward-looking exposures (future variants, continued supply-chain pressure, possible intensification of government restrictions).  The company repeatedly characterises the threat as potentially “material” and “global,” satisfying the threshold for high-severity risk.  Although some passages note mitigating factors—vaccination progress, resumed away-from-home traffic, internal knowledge-sharing, and no *current* material manufacturing interruptions—these are framed as partial, uncertain offsets rather than full neutralisers.  Under the Time Decay Principle, the pandemic falls within the 0-3-year “recent” window, so scores can legitimately reach the 7-10 range when language is direct, impact is already observed and geographic scope is worldwide; more qualified or mitigated statements warrant mid-range scores.  The micro-scorecards below reflect this calibration sentence by sentence.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic and related ongoing impacts may have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial condition and cash flows.

components.reason: Directly attributes potential harm to COVID-19.
Uses strong, finance-oriented wording: 'material adverse effect'.
Covers multiple financial dimensions (operations, condition, cash flows).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Explicit, company-level warning of material impact across key financial metrics; recent event => high score.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic and the related actions by governments around the world to attempt to contain the spread of the virus have negatively impacted, and could continue to negatively impact, our business globally.

components.reason: States both realised and prospective negative impact.
Links risk to external governmental actions (adds uncertainty).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Declares actual damage and ongoing exposure on a global scale.

evidence_list.snippet: Our recovery has been asynchronous and the full extent to which the COVID-19 pandemic will affect our results of operations, financial condition and cash flows will depend on future developments that are highly uncertain and cannot be predicted, including, among others, new information which may emerge concerning the pandemic, vaccine adoption rates (including boosters) and the effectiveness of vaccines in limiting or stopping the spread of COVID-19, either over the long term or against new, emerging variants of COVID-19, and any related actions by governments.

components.reason: Acknowledges uncertain, potentially large future impacts.
Lists multiple uncertainty drivers (variants, vaccine uptake, government action).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking uncertainty flagged, but impact not quantified; mid-level severity.

evidence_list.snippet: The extent and nature of government actions related to the COVID-19 pandemic varied throughout 2020 and 2021 based upon the then-current extent and severity of the COVID-19 pandemic within the respective markets.

components.reason: Notes variability of regulatory environment, implying operational unpredictability.
References multi-year timeline of changing severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Descriptive of shifting risk context; lower direct severity.

evidence_list.snippet: At times we experienced a decrease in sales of certain of our products in markets around the world, including consumer demand shifting to more at-home consumption versus away-from-home consumption.

components.reason: Identifies fundamental shift in consumer demand patterns.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete historic impact on sales and consumer behaviour earns high score.

evidence_list.snippet: While in 2021 we have experienced improved trends in away-from-home channels and improved margins, if COVID-19 infection rates increase, the pandemic intensifies or expands geographically, or continued efforts to curb the pandemic are ineffective, the negative impacts of the pandemic on our sales could be more prolonged and may become more severe than we are currently experiencing.

components.reason: Admits potential for prolonged and more severe sales hit.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Future-risk emphasis balanced by acknowledgement of some recovery.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition, continuing economic and political uncertainties, such as increased unemployment, decreases in disposable income, declines in consumer confidence, or economic slowdowns or recessions in any of our major markets, may slow down or prevent the recovery of the demand for our products or may erode such demand.

components.reason: Links pandemic-driven macro factors to demand risk.
Potential erosion of demand across major markets.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights secondary economic knock-on effects; moderate severity.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has disrupted and could continue to disrupt our global supply chain .
evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strong, concise declaration of ongoing worldwide supply-chain risk.

evidence_list.snippet: We and our bottling partners have experienced temporary disruptions in certain of our operations; delays in delivery of concentrates, ingredients, packaging and equipment; temporary plant closures; production slowdowns; and difficulty or delays in sourcing key ingredients and beverage containers.

components.reason: Evidence of real disruptions already occurred.
Covers essential inputs and production stages.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Enumerates tangible bottleneck incidents—high severity.

evidence_list.snippet: We and our bottling partners may face similar disruptions in the future, which may increase supply chain and packaging costs, or may result in an inability to secure key ingredients and inputs, which could cause delays in delivering our products to our customers and consumers.

components.reason: Projects cost inflation and delivery delays.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking cost and availability concerns; moderate-high risk.

evidence_list.snippet: Although we are unable to predict the impact on our ability to source materials in the future, we expect supply chain pressures to continue into 2022.

components.reason: Admits inability to predict full impact (uncertainty).
Explicit expectation of continued pressure in the near term.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges ongoing near-term sourcing pressure; some uncertainty tempers score.

evidence_list.snippet: In addition to the above risks, the COVID-19 pandemic may exacerbate other risks related to our business, including risks related to changes in the retail landscape or the loss of key retail or foodservice customers; fluctuations in input costs, inflation rates, and foreign currency exchange rates; and the ability of third-party service providers and business partners to fulfill their 11 respective commitments and responsibilities to us in a timely manner and in accordance with the agreed-upon terms.

components.reason: Identifies pandemic as multiplier of multiple existing risks.
Covers retail, cost and partner-execution dimensions.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Frames COVID-19 as risk amplifier across several areas.

evidence_list.snippet: The continuing evolution of the pandemic may also present risks not currently known to us.
evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Generic uncertainty note; limited specificity yields lower score.

evidence_list.snippet: Throughout 2021, the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and the related actions by governments around the world to attempt to contain the spread of the virus continued to impact our business globally.
evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Recent year, worldwide impact and policy link => high score.

evidence_list.snippet: In particular, the number of people contracting COVID-19 and the preventive measures taken to contain COVID-19, including the spread of new variants, negatively impacted our unit case volume and increased our costs to manufacture and distribute our products.

components.reason: Attributes cause to variants and preventive measures.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct, multi-metric negative impact tied to pandemic variants.

evidence_list.snippet: Our price, product and geographic mix was also negatively impacted, primarily due to unfavorable channel and product mix as consumer demand shifted to more at-home consumption versus away-from-home consumption.

components.reason: Details adverse mix effects on revenue drivers.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific commercial mix deterioration; high but not maximal.

evidence_list.snippet: However, the timing and number of people receiving vaccinations, the governmental actions to reopen certain economies around the world, and the substance and pace of the economic recovery favorably impacted our business when compared to 2020.
evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Purely mitigating; reduces overall severity (floor at 0 in principle, but negative kept to show offset).

evidence_list.snippet: While uncertainties caused by the COVID-19 pandemic remain, and factors such as the state of the supply chain, labor shortages and the inflationary environment are likely to impact the pace of the economic recovery, we expect to continue to see improvements in our business as we continue to learn and adapt to the ever-changing environment.

components.reason: Admits persistent uncertainties incl. supply chain & labour shortages.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Risk present but partially offset by expected adaptation.

evidence_list.snippet: The Company’s priorities during the COVID-19 pandemic and related business disruptions are ensuring the health and safety of our employees; supporting and making a difference in the communities we serve; keeping our brands in supply; maintaining the quality and safety of our products; and serving our customers across all channels as they adapt to the shifting demands of consumers during the pandemic.

components.reason: Focuses on response priorities rather than risk exposure (mitigating).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Mainly mitigation narrative; lowers aggregate risk tone.

evidence_list.snippet: Throughout the pandemic, business continuity and adapting to the needs of our customers have been critical.
evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Acknowledges challenge but without detailing severity.

evidence_list.snippet: We have developed systemwide knowledge-sharing routines and processes, which include the management of any supply chain challenges.
evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Pure mitigation; subtracts from overall risk.

evidence_list.snippet: As of the date of this filing, while we have experienced some temporary supply chain disruptions, there has been no material impact, and we do not foresee a material impact, on our and our bottling partners’ ability to manufacture or distribute our products.
evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Strong mitigating statement outweighs minor acknowledgment.

evidence_list.snippet: An increase in the cost, a sustained interruption in the supply, or a shortage of some of these ingredients, other raw materials, packaging materials, aluminum cans and other containers that may be caused by changes in or the enactment of new laws and regulations; a deterioration of our or our bottling partners’ relationships with suppliers; supplier quality and reliability issues; trade disruptions; changes in supply chain; and increases in tariffs; or events such as natural disasters, widespread outbreaks of infectious diseases (such as the COVID-19 pandemic), power outages, labor strikes, political uncertainties or governmental instability, or the like could negatively impact our net operating revenues and profits.

components.reason: Includes COVID-19 among potential triggers for supply interruptions.
Connects to negative revenue and profit impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Pandemic listed as one of several hazards; moderate incremental risk.
